newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy transport unions start wave of strikes.
newsitem.headline: Italy transport unions start wave of strikes.

text.p: Transport unions launched the first in a wave of strikes on Tuesday that looks set to hamper travel in Italy over the next two weeks.
Train, bus, ferry and air unions have called some 26 strikes between now and May 4 as part of long-running disputes over contract renewal and a reorganisation of the transport sector.

Bus, tram and metro travel was disrupted across the country by a series of staggered strikes to put pressure on the government and local authorities to renew contracts which expired some 15 months ago.
Rome was particularly hard hit as drivers extended their walkout to protest against a management decision to suspend the ringleaders of a recent wildcat strike.
Major railway unions will pick up the baton at 1900 GMT, with a 24-hour protest against government plans for the sector, saying the state wants to boost road traffic at the expense of train travel.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government cut subsidies to the state railway in the 1997 budget, but at the same time introduced incentives for people to buy new cars.
The state railways said they would guarantee scheduled long-haul train journeys and key commuter links.
Ferry unions have announced industrial action for later in the month, while flights are also threatened by a number of regional strikes called by various labour groups.
